subject: Cedar model elevated 5xx wave — customer update & remediation follow-up
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: acme-platform-support@acme-retail.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Cedar model elevated 5xx observed — immediate mitigation and next steps

Hi Daniel —

Wanted to reach out proactively: on Sunday evening we observed an elevated rate of 5xx and timeout responses for requests routed to the cedar-2.1 model you have pinned for product catalog summarization. The first spike started ~2026-11-29T22:40Z and we saw intermittent failures through the early hours. Impact was primarily generation timeouts and a small fraction (~2.1%) of 503/504 responses for requests with long context histories.

What we did immediately:
- Shifted live traffic away from cedar-2.1 to cedar-lite-1.0 (compatible fallback) for read-heavy endpoints to reduce customer-facing errors.
- Applied a temporary rate cap per API key to smooth the backend queueing and avoid KV-cache thrash on the serving nodes.
- Kicked off a dedicated ops investigation (Ben + Platform) and traced a correlation to a recent kernel optimization that changes KV eviction ordering under long prefix sequences.

Customer impact (short summary):
- Some requests returned 5xx/timeouts for ~3 hours; retrying succeeded in most cases after fallback.
- No data loss reported.

Next steps from our side:
1) We are compiling an RCA and will share the draft by Wednesday (2026-12-02).
2) Temporary mitigations remain in place until we roll a targeted fix to the cedar runtime.
3) We'll propose a compensation credit for affected API calls; Marissa is aligning numbers.

Attachments: short log excerpt and an incident checklist are attached.

I know this caused disruption to your nightly batch jobs — I apologize. We aim to minimize recurrence and will prioritize any requested rollback or longer-term configuration changes you want.

If you prefer a quick call now, I can join with engineering. Otherwise we will follow up in-thread with the RCA draft and next steps.

Thanks,
Rafael
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs:
- support_log_snippet.txt (text excerpt of sampled request/response latencies)
- cedar-rca-summary.pdf (one-page incident checklist)
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-retail.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:39:21 -0800
Subject: Re: Cedar model elevated 5xx observed — immediate mitigation and next steps

Rafael —

Thanks for the heads up and for failing over to cedar-lite. We saw our ETL job report a large number of retries and delays; fortunately the fallback avoided failures in production dashboards but latency went up. Two quick asks:

1) Can you confirm whether any inference payloads were retried by Redwood (server-side) or if retries were client-side? We need to know for idempotency implications.
2) Please include the list of affected API keys and a rough estimate of token volume for crediting.

If you have a proposed timeline for the fix and when we can expect cedar-2.1 fully restored, that would help scheduling our next nightly run. We can hop on a call if needed.

—Daniel
Senior Engineering Manager
Acme Retail
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cedar model elevated 5xx observed — immediate mitigation and next steps

Daniel —

Quick answers to your asks: 
- No server-side automatic retries were introduced by Redwood. The bulk of the successful completions after the spike were because of the manual routing change to cedar-lite and some client retries. We did not perform any opaque replays of your requests.
- Marissa is pulling the API key usage and token counts now; preliminary estimate is ~1.2M tokens across your affected keys during the 3-hour window. We will provide a detailed accounting in the RCA.

Status update on remediation:
- Engineering (Ben) isolated the trigger to a kernel scheduling optimization deployed 11/27 that interacts poorly with long KV histories, causing occasional blocking in the attention cache path and then timeouts when eviction and rehydration occur concurrently.
- We have a targeted patch that reverts the specific scheduling heuristic and includes additional guards to prevent KV thrash. We validated the patch in staging with a long-prefix workload (mirrors Acme’s pattern) and saw request success rates restored to baseline.
- Planned rollout: staged deploy starting 2026-12-02 02:00 PT with canary traffic for 30 minutes, then progressive ramp if metrics look good.

Proposed customer-facing items:
1) RCA draft (we'll share): cause, timeline, mitigations, and long-term prevention.
2) Credits: Marissa will propose credit amounts based on token accounting and SLA terms.
3) Optional: we can schedule an architecture review to discuss pinning strategies and fallback policy to avoid similar pain during future runtime changes.

Would you like us to proceed with the 12/02 canary rollout? We're holding to coordinate with you if you'd prefer a maintenance window.

Regards,
Rafael

---
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Cedar incident — RCA draft & proposed credits

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for your patience. Attached is a short RCA draft (cedar-rca-summary.pdf) and a support log excerpt (support_log_snippet.txt) pulled from the affected node set. Summary highlights below: 

- Incident window: 2026-11-29T22:40Z -> 2026-11-30T01:50Z (peak errors 22:55Z–23:30Z).
- Root cause: interaction between a kernel-level scheduling optimization (deployed 2026-11-27) and long KV cache histories used by cedar-2.1, leading to transient blocking and subsequent request timeouts.
- Customer impact (Acme Retail): ~2.1% of requests returned 5xx/timeouts during peak; estimated token volume impacted 1,245,000 tokens across three API keys.
- Immediate remediation: traffic reroute to cedar-lite-1.0, temporary per-key rate caps, rollback of the scheduling heuristic in the serving runtime.
- Long-term actions: additional automated canary scenarios for long-prefix KV churn, improved metric instrumentation around KV eviction latencies, and a post-deploy smoke test for affected models.

Proposed customer credit: a one-time credit equivalent to 1.5x the estimated token cost for the impacted window, applied against your next invoice. We can revise if you prefer a different reconciliation method.

Planned timeline: the rollback was canaried 2026-12-02 02:00 PT and fully ramped after checks — we observed error rates back to baseline within 25 minutes of canary start.

If this looks good, we'll finalize the RCA and apply the credit. If you'd like a short sync to walk through details, Rafael and Ben are available tomorrow morning PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs included:
- cedar-rca-summary.pdf (RCA draft, 2 pages)
- support_log_snippet.txt (sampled logs; timestamps and trace IDs)
